To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel neural audio synthesis architecture and demonstrate it with a large-scale dataset and qualitative and quantitative results.
We introduce a new WaveNet-style model and a new dataset that together allow for the synthesis of high-quality musical notes with controllable timbre.

(a) we introduce a powerful new WaveNets-style autoencoder that conditions on temporal codes learned directly from the raw audio signal, (b) we introduce NSynth - a large-scale and highly curated musical note dataset, and (c) we demonstrate improved qualitative performance of our autoencoder on NSynth compared to a spectral autoencoder baseline, and that the model learns to morph in timbre to interpolate between musical notes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three questions: (a) Can a generative model learn to synthesize high-fidelity audio from raw waveforms? (b) Can we build a dataset that is large enough to support such modeling? (c) What can we do with such a model?

the development of a generative model for raw audio that is capable of synthesizing high-fidelity audio samples of musical notes, and with the creation of a dataset that will enable future progress in this area.
the development of new models and datasets for the synthesis of raw audio signals and their application to musical timbre.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper proposes an interesting new approach to learning representations for raw audio waveforms that can be useful for a variety of applications.
the WaveNet autoencoders can learn a manifold of embeddings for audio synthesis.
we introduce a new WaveNet autoencoder architecture for modeling audio, and demonstrate its use on the NSynth dataset of music notes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to generate new musical notes by learning a latent representation of audio waveforms and then using that to synthesize novel sounds.
we have developed a novel generative model that can learn the latent representation of raw audio waveforms, and can generate realistic samples of audio waveforms conditioned on this latent space.
we have created a dataset that is useful for training a model that can generate high quality musical notes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

WaveNet-style autoencoders can be used to synthesize audio with high-quality and high-fidelity, and that the NSynth dataset enables this technology to be used to create new types and styles of sounds.
WaveNet autoencoders are a promising approach for learning representations of raw audio, and that NSynth will be a valuable resource for the machine learning community.
the WaveNet autoencoders can learn a powerful representation of audio, and that large-scale high-quality datasets are essential to enable progress in audio synthesis.
